A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and GraphNormv2 method. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including identification of added and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments in Table 1 and numerical investigations of linear and nonlinear GNN dynamics in Figure 1 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original classification results and reports additional baseline, depth, Cornell and GraphSAGE experiments in Table 1 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The GraphNormv2 formula, learned projection, eigenvector basis augmented to represent the all-ones vector, scaling and affine parameters remain unchanged in Section 5.2. Additional backbones evaluate the existing method rather than introduce a new component.

E1.justification: v3 adds Cornell as a heterophilic node-classification benchmark while retaining the six previously evaluated datasets and both classification tasks. PubMed disappears from the dataset-statistics table, but neither version reports PubMed outcomes, so removal of evaluated coverage is not established.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GroupNorm and PowerEmbed comparisons across the existing GCN, GAT and GIN experiments. Figure 1 replaces BatchNorm without centering with PowerEmbed. These materially revise the evaluated comparator sets rather than merely add citations.

E3.justification: The main dynamics experiment changes from distance to the all-ones subspace to squared distance to the dominant-eigenvector subspace. v3 also adds 20-layer ogbn-arxiv evaluations, GraphSAGE configurations, a depth sweep and Cornell evaluation using ten fixed PyG splits. The existing classification experiments retain their stated cross-validation, optimizer, epoch budget and hyperparameter grid.

E4.justification: v3 revises the main GCN collapse analysis and adds classification accuracy versus depth for GraphNormv2, GroupNorm and BatchNorm in Appendix D.1. Conversely, v1's Appendix C Figures 2–4, containing detailed linear/nonlinear convergence diagnostics for GCN, GIN and GAT, are removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: Figure 1 newly specifies averaging over ten independent trials and displays variability bands; v1 did not provide this repetition disclosure or uncertainty display for that analysis. The new depth plot explicitly reports standard deviations. Table 1 retains its existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting over ten trials and five folds; an increase in run counts is not established.

E6.justification: All shared Table 1 means and standard deviations are unchanged, but added baseline rows and 20-layer ogbn-arxiv results substantially expand the evidence. New competitors alter rankings: GroupNorm scores 87.4 on GAT/Cora versus GraphNormv2's retained 86.3. Appendix D adds Cornell, GraphSAGE and depth results. Figure 1 now detects vanilla GCN collapse under the revised metric, which is not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: v3 introduces the general squared-distance measure μ_v, Appendix A.2's metric-equivalence arguments and Lemma B.1, and strengthens or generalizes the residual and BatchNorm bounds. It removes v1 Appendix B.8's result for applying nonlinearity after BatchNorm and explicitly assumes normalized initial features. Proposition 5.1 restricts tau from nonzero to positive, although its appendix restatement retains the old condition. These substantially change formal scope and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and discussion retain the same central claims: residual connections and normalization prevent collapse through different mechanisms, centering can distort graph information, and GraphNormv2 addresses this problem effectively. The broader theory and experiments develop these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds an explicit interpretation that the theory applies across homophilic and heterophilic settings and attributes poor BatchNorm/GraphNorm performance with GraphSAGE to centering its dominant all-ones eigenvector. Section 4.2 also explicitly describes the limiting normalized computation as memoryless. The earlier qualification concerning GAT remains.

D1.justification: v3 replaces v1's future-release statement and generic GitHub link with reported availability at a specific repository. A new reproducibility section identifies ablation_study.ipynb, graph_level_norm.sh and node_level_norm.sh as reproduction entry points. Existing training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting PowerEmbed, GroupNorm, GraphSAGE, Cornell and the discussion of oversmoothing measures. New Remark 4.4 explicitly credits Chen et al. (2020) with Krylov-subspace attainability and identifies the converse containment result as the additional contribution. The main related-work discussion otherwise remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the abstract's ending, Section 4's explanatory framing and selected interpretation paragraphs. Section 4.3 becomes an unnumbered comparison paragraph, and reproducibility, acknowledgements and new appendix subsections are introduced. Citation style changes to author-year, but most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised axes, variability bands and bar displays for rank. Table 1 gains baseline rows and a depth-specific dataset column. Three appendix diagnostic figures disappear, while a new depth figure and two classification tables are added. The conference template also changes headings, headers and page layout.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons and concrete reproduction instructions improve empirical scrutiny. However, v1's positivity argument is replaced by a stronger lower-bound claim whose new proof contains a contradictory inequality in Equation 11. New Appendix A.2 also equates an unsquared distance with μ_v despite Equation 3 defining it as squared distance. These problems in the central theoretical extension, together with removed diagnostic plots, prevent a reliable net judgment against the empirical and reproducibility gains.
